title: Hybrid clock coordinator and slice defragmentation for mixed H100/L40S/A10 fleets
creator: Priya Nair
description: Problem: In mixed-GPU clusters (H100, L40S, A10) we observe tail-latency regressions and capacity fragmentation when small MIG slices are over-provisioned with aggressive clocks. Current per-card clock policies and the kernel selector do not account for cross-slice thermal and power coupling, leading to suboptimal scheduling decisions for prefill vs. decode phases. Goal: Implement a hybrid clock coordination layer plus a slice defragmentation controller that (1) exposes a low-latency API for the runtime kernel selector to query expected effective clocks per slice, (2) aggregates slice usage to perform opportunistic defragmentation (migrate or consolidate slices before large prefill batches), and (3) integrates with kernel selection heuristics to prefer quantized/packed kernels on constrained slices while prioritizing full-precision kernels on warmed/coalesced groups.
tasks: Spike: microbench H100/L40S/A10 at combinations of MIG sizes (1g/2g/3g) and clock domains to map latency vs power (Priya) - DONE
Design: API contract for hybrid clock coordinator and runtime query endpoint (Miguel + EngArch) - In Review
Implement: coordinator service that watches telemetry (temp, power cap, active_warps) and computes effective_clock_hint per slice
Integrate: kernel selector hook to consult effective_clock_hint and fallback to smaller-kernel packing for decode paths
Implement: defragmentation controller with safe migration plan (drain -> migrate KV cache -> resume) for prefill windows
E2E tests: regression harness with synthetic traffic (prefill-heavy, decode-heavy, mixed) and latency/throughput assertions
Dashboard: add per-slice effective_clock and fragmentation score to Console runtime dashboard
acceptance_criteria: P99 prefill latency improves by >= 15% on mixed fleets compared to baseline under identical traffic patterns
Average token cost decreases by >= 6% due to improved kernel packing in constrained scenarios
No increases in OOM/eviction rate during defragmentation operations in 95% of synthetic runs
Kernel selector falls back to packed/quantized kernels only when effective_clock_hint < threshold documented in design
Dashboard surfaces effective_clock_hint and fragmentation score; SRE and PM sign-off on observability
decisions: Use a centralized coordinator per rack (not per-host) to minimize oscillation and enable coalescing across MIG slices on colocated cards
Coordinator exposes a read-only gRPC endpoint for runtime (no write controls to change clocks directly) — clock adjustments remain an ops action for now
Defragmentation will prefer live migration of lightweight KV cache and draining for pinned session workloads; hard migrations for long-running sessions are out of scope
Kernel selector will use a three-tier heuristic: GOLD (full kernels), SILVER (packed kernels), BRONZE (quantized kernels) based on effective_clock_hint and thermal slope
bench_results: 2026-03-05 spike: H100 1g @ base clock vs boosted clock => prefill p99 reduced 18% when coalesced (single-card warmup)
2026-03-07 mixed fleet synthetic: without coordinator P99=512ms, with coordinator+defrag P99=412ms under same arrival curve
2026-03-09 kernel-packer experiment: token cost down 7% on A10-heavy runs when runtime favors packed kernel selection
comments: 2026-03-03 Priya Nair: Completed initial power/latency sweep across H100/L40S/A10. Observed strong non-linear coupling between adjacent slices at boosted clocks — suggests coordinator should model pairwise thermal influence.
2026-03-05 Miguel Santos: Implemented prototype gRPC contract and local simulator. Pushed simulator artefacts to runtime repo under tests/simulators/clock_coordinator.

2026-03-08 Priya Nair: Kernel selector patch (#8721) shows correct SILVER fallbacks during low effective_clock_hint windows. Need to harden selection thresholds and add hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping.
2026-03-10 EngArch review: Prefer rack-level coordinator but limit decision velocity to reduce churn. Action: add rate-limiter and 90s stabilization window to defrag planner.
2026-03-12 SRE Owen Li: Agreed on observability hooks. Request adding alert when defrag migrations exceed 3 per-hour per-rack.
notes: Risk: Live migration of KV caches may add tail latency spikes. Mitigation: perform migration during cool-down windows and only when predicted benefit > cost model threshold.
Operational: For Private customers with strict upgrade windows, coordinator will be disabled by default behind feature flag ('slice_defrag_enabled').
Follow-up: After rollout, schedule a runbook update and one-week performance sweep during business hours to validate production behavior.
